tasks.short: Review till exception reports and camera footage, weigh proportionality and decide to investigate, interview staff and vendors, check vendor invoices against deliveries, and judge the outcome.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist reviews till exception reports for voids, refunds and discounts in spreadsheets
Loss prevention specialist searches camera footage for the transactions
Loss prevention specialist weighs proportionality and decides to investigate suspected internal theft
Loss prevention specialist interviews staff, witnesses and vendors
Loss prevention specialist checks vendor invoices against deliveries for vendor fraud
Loss prevention specialist judges intent and decides the outcome

tasks.design: Fixed rules in the till system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) report unusual voids, refunds and discounts per till, and each flagged transaction links to the camera footage at that till and time, so the specialist does not build spreadsheets or scroll recordings. Ledger queries in finance ({ERP}) list duplicate vendor payments and deliveries short of the invoice. Weighing proportionality, interviewing and judging intent stay with the specialist. No software analyses gestures or faces, and no person is scored.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exceptions were compiled in spreadsheets and footage searched by time by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Till systems report exceptions and can link transactions to camera footage.
tasks.still_hard: Most flagged transactions have innocent causes.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in an interview that the story does not fit the till record.
tasks.altitude: The specialist starts from flagged cases instead of compiling data.

reach.learn: Whether losses at the till fall.

evidence.claim: Till systems can report exceptions and link transactions to camera footage; ledger queries find duplicate payments.
The private investigators' privacy code requires the least intrusive method, with proportionality weighed first.
Shop cameras and loss analytics also watch staff; works council consent comes first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the suspicion or report to the outcome decided; dismissal and prosecution are outside.
Input contract: till and camera clocks aligned; fallback is spreadsheets and scrolling.
No staff are flagged by name without the specialist's review.
Works council consent and a DPIA come before use.

Weighing, interviewing and judging keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 because the exception list replaces building spreadsheets and reviewing each flag stays; s2 keeps 50 because footage opens at the flagged moment and watching it stays; s5 keeps 40 because the ledger lists mismatches and checking each stays.
research_questions: How many flagged transactions turn out to be theft?

incremental.description: Loss prevention specialist closes flags with innocent causes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: till and camera clocks drift, so footage is still scrolled, and the rules flag many normal transactions (16.0); high: clocks aligned and rules tuned (27.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile loss figures, analyse where losses occur, agree measures with store managers, audit stores for compliance, and write audit reports.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist compiles loss figures from stock counts and incident logs
Loss prevention specialist analyses where property or financial losses occur
Loss prevention specialist agrees processes to reduce losses with store managers
Loss prevention specialist audits stores for compliance with procedures
Loss prevention specialist writes audit reports from paper checklists

tasks.design: A dashboard ({BI}) over stock count results and the incident register shows losses per store, department and cause, so the specialist does not compile spreadsheets. Store audits are done on a tablet checklist that produces the report. Analysing losses, agreeing measures with store managers and auditing stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loss figures were compiled from separate files and audits written up from paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards over stock and incident data; tablet audit checklists.
tasks.still_hard: Unknown loss cannot be split between theft and errors.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a store manager to change a habit that causes losses.
tasks.altitude: The specialist analyses instead of compiling.

reach.learn: Whether losses per cause are visible.

evidence.claim: Dashboards can combine stock count results and incident registers; tablet checklists produce audit reports.

assumptions: Boundary: from period figures to the audit report; store investments are outside.
Input contract: stock counts and incidents in systems; fallback is spreadsheets.
Analysis and agreement stay with the specialist.
Losses are shown per store, not per employee.
research_questions: Do losses fall in stores with agreed measures?

incremental.description: Loss prevention specialist keeps the audit checklist current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about half of the stores log incidents outside the register and audit on paper, so figures are still compiled and reports typed (11.2); high: all stores in the register and on tablets (23.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compare stock counts with system stock, recount suspect items, investigate causes of shortages, write the shortage report, check it, and send it to management.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist compares stock counts with system stock in spreadsheets
Loss prevention specialist recounts suspect items on the shop floor
Loss prevention specialist identifies the causes of merchandise or stock shortages
Loss prevention specialist writes the shortage report
Loss prevention specialist checks the final report: variances, causes, actions and the store and finance managers it goes to
Loss prevention specialist sends the checked report to store and finance management: by e-mail today, by one send from the stock system after the change

tasks.design: The stock system ({ERP}) compares count results with system stock and lists variances above a set value per item, so the specialist does not build spreadsheets. The shortage report is generated from the variance list with fields for cause and action. The specialist recounts, identifies causes and checks the report; the specialist checks the final report and its recipients and sends it to store and finance management from the system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts and system stock were compared in spreadsheets and reports written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Stock systems produce variance lists and report templates.
tasks.still_hard: Booking errors look like theft until checked.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a shortage follows one delivery driver's route.
tasks.altitude: The specialist investigates variances instead of finding them.

reach.learn: Whether shortages are explained before closing.

evidence.claim: Stock systems can compare count results with system stock and list variances.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock count to shortages reported; booking the loss is outside.
Input contract: count results entered in the stock system; fallback is spreadsheets.

Recounting, identifying causes and checking the report keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for reading the variance list; s4 keeps 50 because variances fill in and the specialist writes causes and actions; sending keeps 20.
research_questions: Are more shortages explained before period close?

incremental.description: Loss prevention specialist sets variance thresholds per item group.

approvals.approved_version: The shortage report exactly as checked by the specialist in s5, sent once from the stock system to the store manager and finance management named there; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many stores enter counts late or outside the stock system, so variances are still compared in spreadsheets (20.0); high: counts entered in the system (32.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Log incidents, write investigation reports, check them, send them to store management, inform the person investigated, and keep and delete files on time.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist logs security-related incidents: in a spreadsheet today, in the case register's fields after the change
Loss prevention specialist writes reports on investigations

loop.input: The case register fields (assignment, method and reason, findings, photos) and the specialist's notes.
loop.output: A draft narrative for the findings section; the other sections are filled from the fields.
loop.check: Code checks every name, date, place and amount in the narrative against the case register and drops sentences that do not match. The specialist reads each drafted finding against their notes and the evidence and removes or rewrites any finding they do not support; unclear findings are written by hand.
loop.stop: One draft per report; if the specialist rejects it, they write the narrative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Findings must be told in sequence and context; fields alone do not explain what happened.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist checks the final report: findings, the person and facts named, and the store manager it goes to
Loss prevention specialist sends the checked report to store management: by e-mail today, by one send from the register after the change
Loss prevention specialist informs the person investigated
Loss prevention specialist maintains documentation and deletes files after the retention period

tasks.design: The specialist logs incidents in one case register ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with the fields the privacy code requires instead of a spreadsheet; this first record keeps its time. A template fills the report from the fields, and a bounded step drafts the findings narrative from the specialist's notes; code checks every name, date and amount against the register, and the specialist reads each finding against the notes and evidence. The specialist checks the final report and its recipient and sends it to store management from the register. The register lists files due for deletion under the retention rules. Informing the person investigated stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents sat in spreadsheets and reports were written from scratch and mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Case registers with fixed fields; language models draft narratives that code checks against fields.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted narratives can add detail the specialist did not record.
tasks.human_edge: Writing findings fairly about a colleague's possible theft.
tasks.altitude: The specialist edits and checks instead of writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether reports are complete and consistent.

evidence.claim: The privacy code fixes dossier fields (assignment, method and reason, findings, photos), keeps register data one to five years, and requires telling the person investigated.
Language models can draft narratives from notes; code can check names, dates and amounts against fields.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incident to files maintained; legal proceedings are outside.
Input contract: register fields filled as work happens; fallback is spreadsheets and templates.

The specialist reads and approves every report. Logging, checking and informing the person keep their full time; s2 keeps 70 because facts fill from the fields and the specialist reads and edits the drafted findings; sending keeps 20; s6 keeps 20 for confirming listed deletions and keeping the file.
No personal data leave the organisation's environment in the drafting step.
research_questions: How often does the check drop a sentence?

already_counted.description: Loss prevention specialist edits drafted narratives.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: confirming deletions listed by the register is kept in s6.

approvals.approved_version: The investigation report exactly as checked by the specialist in s3, sent once from the register to the store manager named there; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most cases are complex, so drafted findings are mostly rewritten (22.0); high: routine incident reports where drafts are mostly kept (28.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The loss prevention specialist keeps weighing proportionality, interviewing, judging intent and agreeing measures; spreadsheets, footage searches and report writing shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with more time in stores.
